science.title: Long-term air pollution exposure and childhood ADHD prevalence
science.description: Fine particulate air pollution ($$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$) in the United States has fallen by roughly half since 2000, yet health outcomes may reflect pollution exposures accumulated over longer time scales. Using years of U.S. county-level data, we relate annual $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ estimates to birth outcomes, diabetes prevalence, and small-area estimates of childhood attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) across short and long time scales. Whereas associations with low birth weight and the apparent lag pattern for diabetes were substantially attenuated after accounting for county-specific temporal trends, the association between long-term $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ exposure and childhood ADHD prevalence across 3,106 counties remained robust to socioeconomic and demographic adjustment, state-level heterogeneity, alternative exposure periods, and explicit spatial modeling. After accounting for residual spatial dependence, a 1 $$\mu$$g/$$\hbox {m}^3$$ increase in mean $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ exposure over 2005–2015 was associated with a 0.312 percentage-point higher ADHD prevalence (SE = 0.058, $$p < 0.001$$). These results identify a robust ecological association between long-term county-level $$\hbox {PM}_{2.5}$$ exposure and childhood ADHD prevalence across the United States.

science.title: Information reliability and engagement patterns of Alzheimer’s disease-related short videos on Douyin and Bilibili
science.description: Health-related content is increasingly disseminated through short-video platforms. However, the relationship between user engagement and informational reliability remains uncertain. This issue is particularly important for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), where patients and caregivers rely heavily on accessible information. We screened the first 100 search results from each platform and included eligible Alzheimer’s disease-related videos from Douyin and Bilibili. Informational quality was evaluated using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), and the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with high-quality videos (GQS ≥ 3), with sensitivity analyses based on mDISCERN and JAMA thresholds. Overall, informational quality was low to moderate. Uploader expertise was the only consistent independent predictor of high-quality content, with physician-generated videos demonstrating higher reliability and transparency. Engagement metrics were not consistently associated with informational quality, indicating that more popular videos in the sampled search results were not necessarily more reliable or informative.

science.title: UAV image segmentation in complex mining areas by integrating spatially adaptive feature modulation and multi-scale context fusion modules
science.description: To address the misclassification of visually similar ground objects and inaccurate boundary localization caused by background interference, as well as small-object omission, fragmented regions, and incomplete boundaries resulting from scale variations, this study proposes MASwin-Unet for semantic segmentation of complex mining areas. The model incorporates a Spatially Adaptive Feature Modulation Module (SAFM) to suppress background noise and similar-texture interference while enhancing key regions and boundary details. It also introduces a Multi-Scale Context Fusion Module (MSCF) to integrate contextual information across different receptive fields and improve multi-scale feature modeling. An experimental dataset was constructed from UAV imagery of the Dongshan Xiuqing Mining Area, and experiments were also conducted on AeroScapes and LoveDA. MASwin-Unet achieved an OA of 97.18%, a Kappa coefficient of 95.79%, an mIoU of 85.14%, and an mF1 of 90.73%, outperforming BEDSN, FADC, DeepLabV3 + , PSPNet, HRNet, SegFormer, TransUNet, U-Net, and Swin-Unet. The results demonstrate good generalization on public datasets and show that the model effectively reduces similar-object misclassification, small-object omission, and incomplete boundary segmentation in complex UAV scenes.

science.title: Broadening the Okur-Chung syndrome phenotype: adult-onset metabolic features and a contiguous 20p13 deletion in a Turkish multicenter cohort
science.description: Okur-Chung neurodevelopmental syndrome (OCNDS; OMIM #617062) is an ultra-rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by heterozygous CSNK2A1 variants encoding CK2α; although the CSNK2A1 Foundation registry lists more than 350 diagnosed individuals worldwide, individual-level phenotypic data have been published for far fewer, and reports from Türkiye remain scarce. We retrospectively studied nine unrelated Turkish probands (4 F/5 M; 11 months to 23 years) from nine medical genetics centers across four geographic regions of Türkiye, diagnosed by exome sequencing (ES; n = 8) or chromosomal microarray (n = 1). A PRISMA 2020–compliant systematic review (inception–April 2026) provided an individual-level comparator pooled with our cohort (n = 61). Six distinct CSNK2A1 alterations were identified: the recurrent p.(Lys198Arg) p + 1 loop hotspot in 4/9 probands (44.4%); novel/rare p.(Arg195Gln) and p.(Asp156His) missense changes; two nonsense variants (p.(Tyr182Ter), p.(Arg333Ter)); and one ~537 kb heterozygous 20p13 contiguous deletion (arr[GRCh37] 20p13(61568_598427)x1). This proband also represents 20p13 deletion syndrome; previously reported cases of that entity were compared with our cohort. Core OCNDS features (developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, dysmorphism, behavioral disturbance) occurred at frequencies comparable to those in the pooled literature. Adult-onset obesity with type 2 diabetes (2/9) and hypogonadism (2/9), both essentially unreported in the predominantly pediatric pooled literature, were observed in two adolescent/young-adult males (one with p.(Lys198Arg), one with the 20p13 deletion). This series consolidates Lys198 as a recurrent hotspot across ethnically diverse cohorts, extends the structural-variant spectrum with the first Turkish CSNK2A1 contiguous-gene deletion, and supports adult-onset metabolic-reproductive complications as under-recognized OCNDS features. Systematic adolescent and adult metabolic-endocrine surveillance is recommended regardless of variant class.
